A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same principal-agent bandit work. The main text, Table 1, algorithms, equations, and Appendices A-G are readable, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports algorithms, theoretical regret guarantees, and proofs, without original experimental or simulation outcomes. Appendix B's Bernoulli example is an analytical counterexample.

after.justification: v2 remains entirely theoretical, including its appendices. The additional behavioral-science citations do not constitute empirical results produced by this work.

M1.justification: Section 2 replaces the linear agent's ridge regression with unknown regularization parameter by ordinary least squares using a Moore-Penrose inverse, and specifies its initial estimate. The principal's elimination and incentive-search algorithms otherwise retain their procedures after matching renumbered versions.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or conducts empirical task evaluations. The i.i.d. and linear reward cases remain theoretical settings.

E2.justification: Neither version experimentally evaluates baselines. Table 1 retains the same theoretical comparators: Dogan et al. (2023a,b), IPA, and C-IPA from Scheid et al. (2024b).

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental splits, training budgets, evaluation metrics, or testing procedures. The revised linear estimator is a model assumption, not an experimental protocol revision.

E4.justification: Neither version contains ablations, empirical robustness tests, or error analyses. Appendix B retains the same analytical counterexample, and the robustness arguments remain theoretical.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental runs, seeds, error bars, or significance tests. Algorithmic repetitions and concentration bounds concern theoretical guarantees rather than empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: No measured result entries are added, removed, or revised. Table 1 retains the same asymptotic rates after matching algorithm numbers; changes to formal theorem statements are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Most lemmas and proofs are retained. v2 adds an initialization argument in D.1 and restricts the linear confidence event to rounds after phase 1 in G.2. Theorems 4.2 and 5.1 add horizon conditions and omit additive terms retained in their appendix derivations. E.5 also changes the target-arm payment pi_a(t) to the chosen-arm payment pi_At(t), a substantive algebraic revision.

C1.justification: The elimination-framework novelty and leading regret-rate claims remain the same. However, the linear-reward contribution now applies to an OLS-learning agent rather than v1's ridge-learning agent with unknown regularization, narrowing that contribution's scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds behavioral-science motivation for exploration and explains the regret benchmark when exploration prevents realizing the optimal utility. Its conclusion removes v1's conjectured barrier to square-root regret in the linear setting and adds more general exploration-decay rates as future work.

D1.justification: v1 only promises constant modifications for arbitrary initial empirical means in a footnote. v2 Appendix D.1 documents inverse-count incentive adjustments and modified elimination offsets and thresholds for this previously asserted extension. Neither version supplies code or data access information.

R1.justification: v2 substantially broadens positioning through moral-hazard and adverse-selection literature, comparisons with Fiez et al.'s dynamic-preference models and Lin and Chen's learning-agent setting, and cognitive-science motivation. It also removes the Lobel et al. contextual-search citation. This expands the scientific context beyond v1's predominantly bandit-focused discussion.

P1.justification: v2 extensively compresses and rewrites the introduction and algorithm explanations, removes the separate challenge discussion, places exploratory i.i.d. agents before linear rewards, and folds the oracle refinement into Section 4.3. Numerous definitions and algorithm details move to appendices, and acknowledgements and an impact statement are added.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column manuscript to a two-column conference layout. Table 1 is reformatted, most complete algorithm boxes move to appendices, and a new informal Algorithm 2 summarizes the retained exploratory-agent algorithm. The appendix contents page is removed, with extensive changes to display placement.

improvement.justification: v2 provides useful initialization details, a compact algorithm overview, and broader research context. However, it introduces technical inconsistencies: E.5 and F.10 associate the retained Algorithm 5 and Algorithm 6 proofs with mismatched theorem statements, and E.5 replaces the target-arm payment with the chosen-arm payment although exploration can make them differ. The shortened Theorems 4.2 and 5.1 also retain fuller bounds in their proofs. These unresolved issues prevent a reliable judgment that the explanatory gains outweigh the loss of theoretical precision.
